svg.title: Token validation as five gates, and the arrow that must never exist
svg.desc: Five checks stacked in order, each with the response it returns when it fails on the right. One, is there an Authorization Bearer header, since tokens never arrive in the query string; it fails with 401 and the WWW-Authenticate challenge that starts the whole discovery chain. Two, does the token verify, by signature against the issuer keys or by introspection; it fails with 401 and an invalid_token error. Three, is it still inside its lifetime; it fails with 401, and short-lived tokens mean this one is expected. Four, drawn with a terracotta outline and a chip reading the skipped one, is the audience me, compared against the resource you published and nothing else; it fails with 401 because the token was meant for another service, and a server must reject a token that does not name it. Five, does the token carry the scopes this call needs, named all at once in one challenge; it is the only one that fails with 403 and an insufficient_scope error, which tells the client to step up rather than log in again. Past all five, a green box says serve the request, with a note that the access token is handed to the handler. A panel at the foot draws the same call to an upstream API twice: once with the client's own token forwarded, crossed out and marked must not pass it through, and once with a separate token issued to your server, ticked, because there you are an OAuth client and not a proxy.
svg.text: Five gates, two status codes
Every request runs the whole gate. There is no session that remembers the last one.
the check, in order
what you return if it fails
1. Is there an Authorization: Bearer header?
tokens never arrive in the query string
401 WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=
the challenge that starts the whole chain
2. Does it verify?
signature against the issuer keys, or introspection
401 error="invalid_token"
the signature failed, or introspection said no
3. Is it still inside its lifetime?
short-lived tokens are the point; expect to see this one
401 invalid or expired token
the client refreshes and comes straight back
4. Is the audience me?
the resource you published, exactly. Nothing else.
the skipped one
401 a token meant for another service
MUST reject a token that does not name you
5. Does it carry the scopes this call needs?
name every scope the call needs, in one challenge
403 error="insufficient_scope", scope="..."
403 means step up, not log in again
Serve the request
get_access_token() gives the handler the AccessToken
And when your server calls something else
your server
upstream API
the client's own token, forwarded
MUST NOT pass it through
your server
upstream API
a separate token, issued to you
you are an OAuth client here, not a proxy
